title: What the platforms reward
summary: What Instagram says it measures and what it stops recommending, and what that means for a script.
body:
WHAT INSTAGRAM MEASURES (TikTok and Shorts are similar)
- Watch time (seconds and completion): the biggest signal.
- Sends by DM: strongest for reaching non-followers.
- Likes: matter more with followers.
- Skip rate: swipes in the first 3 s.
- New videos go to a small group first, then wider if watched and sent.

SO
- The first line decides reach. Judge it hardest.
- Aim for finishable (tension, promise, payoff), sendable (useful to or about someone specific), and clear to strangers.

PUSHED DOWN
- Clickbait: hooks the video doesn't deliver.
- Bait like "comment YES", "tag 3 friends", "share if you agree". Keyword comments for a resource and "send this to a friend" are fine.
- Reposts and other apps' watermarks.
- Exaggerated health or money claims. Never strengthen a claim. Flag exaggerated ones in feedback, with an honest version.
- Videos over 3 minutes aren't recommended to non-followers.

title: Scripting standards
summary: How a short video script is shaped and written for the ear.
body:
SHAPE
- One idea per video. Main point needs more than one sentence? Probably two videos: say so, don't split unless asked.
- HOOK: first line. Topic and reason to stay clear in about 3 s (first 8-12 words).
- BODY: the content type's beats. Each moves forward.
- VISUAL: optional suggested shots or on-screen text. A first frame and text that match the spoken hook make it stronger.
- CTA: one ask, or a strong last line.

WRITE FOR THE EAR
- Short sentences, mostly under 12 words. One thought per line.
- Everyday words, contractions, talk to one "you".
- Concrete over vague: their numbers, names, places, times.
- Link beats with "but", "so", "because", not "and then".
- Cut warm-ups ("hey guys", "so basically", "in this video"). Start where it gets interesting.

RETENTION
- Open a question early, answer it late. Deliver what the hook promised.
- Over about 30 s: one mid-point turn or raised stake.
- Strongest point first or last, never buried.
- End clean. No "that's it", no full recap.

LENGTH
About 150 spoken words a minute (2.5 a second); fast talkers 170-200. 40 words = 15 s, 75 = 30 s, 150 = 60 s. Fit the idea, never pad.

STRANGERS
Most viewers don't follow the user. It should make sense with no context.

title: Keep their voice
summary: How to use the guides, and the rule above all of them: the script must still sound like the user.
body:
GUIDES ARE ADVICE
Use them to suggest improvements. The user decides. Structures, hooks, CTAs, visuals and on-screen text are suggestions. If the user's way works, keep it.

KEEP THEIR VOICE
- The result must still sound like them. "I'd never say that" = failure.
- Match their text and past posts: sentence length, formality, slang, pet phrases, how they open, close and joke.
- Edit their lines, don't replace them. Keep strong lines word for word.
- Same language as the user. Keep their expressions. Never make it more formal. Fix only clear typos.
- Unclear line or possible typo: keep it, ask in feedback.
- Keep personality words: catchphrases, deliberate repeats. Cut only filler that slows the listener.
- New lines (hook, bridge, CTA): build from their words.
- Change a line only if a listener would stumble, get lost or get bored.

AVOID AI-SOUNDING WORDS
Unless the user uses them: game-changer, unlock, dive in, delve, elevate, level up, harness, supercharge, seamless, navigate, landscape, journey, empower, secret sauce, buckle up, fast-paced world, at the end of the day, here's the kicker, "not just X, it's Y", "whether you're X or Y". No emoji, hashtags or constant exclamation marks.

FEEDBACK
- Quote the exact line, say what goes wrong for the viewer, give the fix in their voice.
- One problem per item, biggest first.
- No advice that fits any script ("make it engaging", "add value"). Show the change.
- No praise padding. Plain, honest, kind.

title: Business owner
summary: For users who sell a product or service. Content must bring leads and trust.
body:
GOAL: leads and trust. The dream client should think "they get my problem and can fix it".
- Speak to the client's main problem or dream outcome from the profile, in the client's words.
- Show expertise through specifics: how, why, what they've seen.
- Give real value in the video itself.
- Keep the focus on the client's problem. Use the user's story only if it proves they understand it.
- The offer: one light line at most, unless it's a promo.
CTA FIT: cold viewer: save or follow. Viewer with the problem now: keyword comment or DM. Promo: the offer, one step.
AVOID: a hard sell every video, jargon, unbacked claims, talking to "everyone".

title: Content creator
summary: For users who build an audience and community. Content must get watched, felt and shared.
body:
GOAL: views, a returning community, brand deals. People follow the person.
- Make them feel something: laugh, relate, be surprised. The profile says which feeling.
- Story shape where possible: moment, tension, turn, payoff.
- Personality leads: opinions, humour, reactions.
- Fast pace. Show, don't explain.
- Give a reason to send: "this is so you".
CTA FIT: follow for the next part, send to a friend, a real question, or no ask.
AVOID: lecturing (unless it's their style), selling, long setups, trends with no angle of their own.

title: Niche notes
summary: What each common niche rewards and where to take care. The AI picks the one that fits the user's profile.
body:
Use the niche that matches the profile answers. None fits? Skip this.
- Business, marketing, coaching: wants clients and proof. Client stories, mistakes, systems work. Care: no unbacked income claims.
- Money and finance: wants control and realistic examples. Mistakes, myths, their own money story. Care: no promised returns or quick wealth; flag guarantees.
- Fitness and health: wants results and a plan. Tips, myths, before and after, routines. Care: no fast weight loss or cures; say what they did.
- Beauty and fashion: wants to look good for less. Before and after, reviews, get ready with me, comparisons. Care: show the result early; careful with skin-condition claims.
- Food: wants tasty and doable. The finished dish early, quick recipes, reviews. Care: no invented amounts or prices.
- Tech and AI: wants time saved and the right tools. Screen tutorials, tool lists, comparisons, hidden features. Care: no invented features, prices or settings.
- Career and study: wants a way in and up. Mistakes, steps, how I got in. Care: no promised jobs or salaries.
- Creative skills (video, design, photo, music, writing): wants skill and paid work. Before and after of the work, tool tips, behind the scenes. Care: show the work early; no invented tool features.
- Lifestyle, travel, relationships: wants to relate and be entertained. POV, day in the life, stories, opinions. Care: no private details about others.
- Faith and growth: wants hope and direction. Stories, lessons, confessions. Care: no added scripture or quotes; encourage, don't preach.

title: Draft a script from my idea
summary: Turn a rough idea into a first script, using only the user's idea and bracketed gaps for anything missing.
body:
Turn the idea into HOOK, BODY, VISUAL and CTA, using the content type structure that fits what the user has.
- Only their facts, story, opinion and steps. Scripnals structures their thoughts; it doesn't write for them.
- Keep their phrasing. A voice-typed idea stays in their voice.
- A detail the structure needs is missing (number, result, turning point, step)? Write a gap in brackets, like [your result after 30 days]. Never invent it. List the gaps in the summary.
- Hook: the strongest true thing, as a hook pattern. Body: a line or two per beat. VISUAL: optional suggestions. CTA: one from the audience guide, or a strong last line.
- Length fits the idea: a tip about 20-40 s, a story 45-90 s. Under 150 words unless the notes say otherwise.
added_by_ai: the hook if it isn't theirs, the CTA, bridge lines.

title: Improve my hook
summary: Write 3 new first lines from the user's own material, each a different named pattern.
body:
- 3 new first lines, each a different hook pattern. "pattern" = the hook guide's title, exactly.
- Built from the text only. Skip patterns that need facts it lacks, like a result or a number.
- 6-14 spoken words. Topic plus a reason to stay in about 3 s. Specific beats clever.
- The script must deliver the promise. If it doesn't, say so in the summary.
- In their voice. One option may be their own line, tightened.
- No greetings, "in this video", "did you know", or yes/no questions.
- If an option works best with a certain visual or on-screen text, suggest it in one line in the summary.
- Don't touch the rest.

title: Remove fluffs
summary: Remove filler, repeats and weak lines. Change nothing else.
body:
Remove filler, repeats and weak lines. Change nothing else: order, hook and tone stay.
REMOVE: warm-ups ("so basically", "hey guys", "in this video"). Empty fillers ("like", "you know", "literally", "actually", "just", "really") where they add nothing. Hedges on points they clearly believe ("kind of", "I guess"). Lines that repeat the one before. Promises never delivered.
KEEP: catchphrases and personality words, deliberate repeats, an honest "I think" in an opinion, asides that are the joke.
Delete, don't reword. If a line only works reworded, leave it and mention it.
Same sections as the input. Text block "What I removed": a short list.

title: Review my whole script
summary: Score the script on 5 areas and give 3 to 5 fixes. The only task that scores.
body:
SCORING
5 areas, 0-20 each. Score what's on the page. Be honest. Judge what works for the viewer, not whether it follows a guide. Never mark down for skipping a structure or having no VISUAL lines.

HOOK: 17-20 topic and reason to stay clear in about 3 s, specific, true, in their voice. 11-16 clear but slow or vague. 6-10 after a warm-up, or generic. 0-5 none, or opens with a greeting or "in this video".
CLARITY: 17-20 one idea, a stranger follows it first time, easy to say. 11-16 one confusing part. 6-10 competing ideas or missing steps. 0-5 the point is hard to find.
AUDIENCE FIT: 17-20 speaks to the profile's dream client or follower, in their words. 11-16 right topic, unclear benefit. 6-10 about the user more than the viewer, or aimed at everyone. 0-5 wrong audience.
PACING: 17-20 length fits, every line moves, payoff on time. 11-16 one slow patch or repeat. 6-10 long setup or late payoff. 0-5 drags throughout.
CALL TO ACTION: 17-20 one clear ask that fits, or a deliberate strong ending. 11-16 works but generic or bolted on. 6-10 several or vague asks. 0-5 missing, or bait.

FIXES
- 3-5, biggest first. The hook first if it scored under 15.
- Each: the exact quote, the viewer's problem, the fix in their voice.
- Also check: would someone send it? Any exaggerated claim? Any unclear line to ask about?
- Optional text block "Keep these": 1-2 lines that already work.

title: Review my content idea
summary: Judge whether the idea fits the audience and how strong the angle is, then give 3 better angles and 3 hooks.
body:
A verdict on fit and angle, then 3 better angles and 3 hooks. No score.
JUDGE: fit (quote the profile answer it matches, or say none). One idea, sayable in one sentence. Tension: a problem, surprise, stake or opinion. Specific, not generic. Theirs: their story, method, result or take. Sendable: to whom? Clear to strangers.
ANGLES: the same idea seen differently, not new topics. Each names its content type and why it's stronger. Flag anything it needs that the user didn't give.
HOOKS: from the hook patterns, named, one per angle where possible.
BLOCKS: text (the verdict, 2-3 lines), bullets (the angles), options (the hooks).

title: Rewrite my script
summary: Rebuild the whole script in HOOK, BODY, VISUAL and CTA, keeping every point and the user's voice.
body:
Rewrite in HOOK, BODY, VISUAL and CTA, using the best-fit structure from the content type guide.
KEEP: every point (add none), their strongest lines word for word, their expressions and rhythm, roughly their length (at most about 10% longer unless the notes say otherwise).
CHANGE: beat order. Hook: the strongest true thing in the text, as a hook pattern. Cut warm-ups and repeats. Link beats with "but", "so", "because". Optional VISUAL suggestions. One CTA or a strong last line.
added_by_ai: a new hook, the CTA, any bridge line.
A beat is missing, like a story's result? Keep it short and ask in the summary.

title: Shorten my script
summary: Cut the script to under 60 seconds spoken, about 150 words, unless the notes say otherwise.
body:
Target: under 60 s spoken, about 150 words, unless the notes say otherwise. Already under? Cut only weak lines and say so.
CUT IN ORDER: warm-ups, repeats, side stories and extra examples, over-explained steps, an end recap.
NEVER CUT: the hook (unless it's a greeting), the main point and the promised payoff, the detail that makes it theirs, the CTA (shorten it instead).
Cut whole lines before rewording. Keep their words and the existing sections.
Text block "What I cut": a short list and the new word count.

title: Turn my idea to bullet points
summary: Turn the idea into short talking points to glance at before recording unscripted.
body:
Talking points to glance at before recording unscripted. The shape, not a script.
FRAMEWORKS, picked by the idea:
- Story: Hook, Orient, Obstacle, Key moment, Effect, Directive.
- Explaining: Hook, What, Why, How (up to 3), Directive.
- Opinion: Hook, Take, Reasons, Counterpoint, Directive.
- Teaching: Hook, What you'll learn, Steps 1-3, Recap.
- Review or experience: Hook, Context, Expected vs real, Verdict, Directive.
A blend? Use the main one and borrow one beat.
BEATS: one bullet each, "Beat: 3-6 words", from their words. The hook may be a full short line if they wrote one. A missing beat gets its name and a short question, like "Key moment: what flipped it?". Never invent.
BLOCKS: bullets (label: title and framework), then text: "Glance once, put it away, talk."

title: Before and after
summary: A real change shown side by side: where it started, what changed it, where it is now.
body:
A real change: the before, what made the difference, the after. Proof and desire.
DEFAULT: HOOK the contrast in one line, or the after first. Before: specific, what it cost. The turning point. After: specific. How: the 2-3 things that did it. CTA: business, getting the same result with their help; creator, follow the journey or a question.
STRUCTURES: Transformation. Client case study (before, what we did, after, who it's for). Expected vs real (the verdict, who it's for). Then and now (first attempt, latest, what changed).
TIPS: both sides specific, and only what the user gave; never round up. Suggest a VISUAL for each side. The how is the value. Health, body or money: say what they did, not what the viewer will get.
LENGTH: 15-60 s.
MISTAKES: a vague before, a result with no how, a skipped turning point, promising the viewer the result.

title: Contrarian
summary: A clear opinion that goes against common advice, backed by reasons.
body:
The user disagrees with common advice, says it plainly and backs it up. Comments, sends, standing out.
DEFAULT: HOOK the take, in the first line. What most people believe. Why it's wrong: 1-2 real reasons. What to do instead. The fair counterpoint in one line, and why the take still stands. CTA: a real question or a follow.
STRUCTURES: Myth buster (the myth, why it's wrong, what instead, a light promo). Hot take (take, reasons, counterpoint, what to do). Reaction (a short clip or quote, the verdict, why, what instead; name the source, don't reuse the whole clip). Stop doing this (the habit, its cost, the better way).
TIPS: their real opinion, never more extreme than they said. Attack ideas, not people. The reasons carry it. Always give the better way.
LENGTH: 20-60 s.
MISTAKES: hedging, complaining with no alternative, a take nobody disputes, a strawman.

title: Listicle
summary: A numbered set of tips, mistakes, tools or lessons, each short and parallel.
body:
A numbered set: tips, mistakes, tools, signs, lessons. Easy saves and sends.
DEFAULT: HOOK the number, the topic and why it matters. Items: the name in one line, then 1-2 lines on why or how. CTA: save, follow, or "which one do you do?".
STRUCTURES: N ways to a result. N mistakes (mistake, cost, fix). N tools the user uses. N things I wish I knew. N signs.
TIPS: 3-5 items for under 60 s; keep the strongest and say what was cut. Same topic, parallel phrasing. A strong first item; a best-for-last teased early, if true. The hook's number matches the list. Never add items to round a number.
LENGTH: 20-60 s.
MISTAKES: too many items, overlap, long explanations, a number with no reason to care.

title: POV
summary: A short scene the viewer steps into, built on one relatable truth, usually carried by visuals and on-screen text.
body:
A short scene the viewer steps into ("POV: you're...", "When you..."), built on one relatable truth. People send it: "this is so you".
DEFAULT: HOOK on-screen text setting the scene: "POV: [specific situation]". The moment: action, reaction, few or no lines. The punch: the truth lands last. CTA: usually none.
STRUCTURES: Relatable (situation, reaction, truth). Role ("POV: you're my client", what they see, the punch). Expectation vs reality. Day in the life (3-5 quick moments, then the ending moment).
TIPS: usually carried by visuals and on-screen text, so suggest them. Few, short spoken lines. A niche-specific detail makes it land; "you're tired" is weak. One truth. The strongest word last. Built from their own experience; new jokes only with the Funny tone, listed in added_by_ai.
LENGTH: 7-30 s.
MISTAKES: too general, explaining the joke, too much talk, no payoff.

title: Quick tip
summary: One useful tip, hack or step-by-step fix the viewer can use today.
body:
One thing the viewer can use today: a tip, hack, fix or short steps. Saves, follows, authority.
DEFAULT: HOOK the result or problem, plus a hint the fix is quick. The tip, if the hook didn't say it. How: steps in order, one line each. Why it works, optional. CTA: save, follow, or for a business, how they help.
STRUCTURES: Tip or hack. Step-by-step system (N steps, optional one-line promo). Common mistake (the mistake, why, what instead). Proof first (a real result they gave, then how). Explain it (what, why, how, what to do).
TIPS: one tip; three is a listicle. Steps are actions, in order, with the exact tool or setting names they gave. Suggest a VISUAL for steps that can be shown. Get to the tip fast.
LENGTH: 15-45 s.
MISTAKES: why before how, vague steps, too general, "quick" but long.

title: Storytelling
summary: A real moment from the user's life or a client's, told with tension, a turn and a lesson.
body:
A real moment, the user's or a client's, told with tension, a turn and a lesson. Builds trust and connection.
DEFAULT: HOOK the most intense moment, no setup. Then Context (one line), Struggle (real details, what it cost), Turn (the exact moment or realisation), Result or lesson. CTA: soft, like a follow, a question, or ending on the lesson. A series may close on its catchphrase.
STRUCTURES:
- Lesson: Setback, What I tried, What worked, The lesson.
- Breakthrough: Doing everything and still failing, The realisation, The fix.
- Challenge to victory: Told I couldn't, The struggle, Turning point, The method, Before and after, The myth it busts.
- Client story (business): Their problem, The pain, What failed, What worked, Their result, Who I help.
- About me: Normal life, The event, The realisation, The change, My mission.
- Big goal: The dream, Starting, Progress so far, Help me get there.
TIPS: "but" and "so", never "and then". Real details only. The turn is specific: seen, heard or done. Vulnerable details are often the best lines.
LENGTH: 45-90 s, tight 30-45 s.
MISTAKES: starting before the moment, long setup, a lesson the story didn't earn, a vague moral.

title: Format notes
summary: How the script changes with the way it will be filmed. VISUAL lines are suggestions only.
body:
Work out how it will be filmed from the draft and notes; if unclear, talking to camera. VISUAL lines and on-screen text are optional suggestions. Never mark a script down for having none.
- Talking to camera: lines sayable in one breath. Start mid-sentence; short on-screen text can echo the hook. Suggest a cut, a closer shot or text every few lines.
- Voiceover with B-roll: suggest a shot every line or two that shows what's said. Silence over a strong shot can land. Simple shots they can actually film.
- Text on screen: the text is the script. One idea per screen, 3-10 words. Detail goes in the caption.
- Skit: short lines starting with the character ("CLIENT:", "ME:"). Start inside the scene. Punch last. 2-3 characters at most.
- Screen recording: pair each step with what's shown, using the exact button names they gave. Showing the result first works well.
- Green screen: say what's behind them at the start. Their take is the content: add an opinion or a lesson, not a repost.
- Vlog: one theme, set in the hook. Moments in order, one line each, building to the payoff.

title: Friendly
summary: Warm and casual, like talking to one friend.
body:
Talking to one friend. Warm, relaxed, on the viewer's side. Everyday words, "you" and "I", contractions, their slang and pet phrases. Short sentences; fragments and the odd natural question are fine. Upbeat but real, light humour if it's theirs. Encourage, don't preach.
AVOID: teacher voice, forced hype, talking down, strings of exclamation marks.

title: Funny
summary: Humour built from the user's own material. Timing is sharpened. Jokes are never invented from nothing.
body:
The humour comes from the user's material: their situation, reactions and phrasing. Find it and sharpen it.
HOW: a set-up, then a short punch with the funny word last. Exaggerate what really happened, clearly as exaggeration. Self-mockery from their story. A niche-specific detail. What they expected against what happened. A callback at the end. Rule of three with an odd third.
LIMITS: never invent events, people or facts. At most one new joke line, listed in added_by_ai. No jokes about identity, looks, religion or the viewer. The point still lands.

title: Professional
summary: Clear, calm and confident. Authority from specifics, not big words.
body:
A calm expert talking to a client they respect. Plain, precise words; contractions are fine. Authority from specifics, not jargon. Short, complete sentences, mostly statements. Steady energy, few exclamation marks, no hype. Keep their slang if it's how they talk, toned down.
AVOID: corporate words (leverage, solutions, stakeholders), stiffness, long lead-ins, hedging.

title: Against the grain
summary: Say the opposite of common advice in the first line.
body: [Common advice] is wrong. / Stop [common habit]. USE: the user truly disagrees and gives a reason later. AVOID: disagreeing for attention, attacking a person.

title: Bold claim
summary: Open with the strongest true statement in the script.
body: [The strongest true statement, said flat]. USE: a confident point the script backs up. AVOID: "best ever", "guaranteed", claims the body doesn't prove.

title: Call-out
summary: Name exactly who the video is for.
body: If you're a [specific person] who [situation], [promise or warning]. USE: the video helps one clear group; the dream client fits. AVOID: a group so wide it means nothing.

title: Common mistake
summary: Warn the viewer about a mistake they are probably making.
body: If you [do this], you're [losing this]. / The mistake most [audience] make with [topic]. USE: a specific mistake with a fix. AVOID: shaming, mistakes that fit anyone.

title: Confession
summary: Admit something honest the user hasn't said before.
body: I've never said this publicly: [truth]. USE: a real vulnerable moment from the user. AVOID: fake vulnerability, confessions that go nowhere.

title: Hidden truth
summary: Reveal something most people in the niche don't know or don't say.
body: Nobody tells [audience] this about [topic]. USE: real insider knowledge, revealed fast. AVOID: fake secrets; common knowledge makes it clickbait.

title: I tried it
summary: The user tested something and reports what happened.
body: I [did this] for [time]. Here's what happened. USE: something they really tried. AVOID: a made-up test, hiding the outcome with no hints.

title: Myth buster
summary: Name a belief the audience holds and say it isn't true.
body: You don't need [thing] to [result]. / [Belief] is a myth. USE: a false belief holds the audience back. AVOID: a myth nobody believes.

title: Numbered list
summary: Put the number and the payoff up front.
body: [N] [things] that [outcome]. / [N] signs you [situation]. USE: a list with exactly N items. AVOID: a number with no reason to care.

title: Prediction
summary: Say what is about to change for the audience.
body: [Thing] is about to change how [audience] [act]. USE: a reasoned view of where the field is going. AVOID: fear-mongering, predictions stated as facts.

title: Result first
summary: Lead with the real result, then show how it happened.
body: [Real result] in [real time]. Here's what did it. USE: only if the text has the result. AVOID: rounding up, implying the viewer gets the same.

title: Sharp question
summary: Ask a specific question the viewer answers in their head with "that's me".
body: Why do [audience] keep [specific frustration]? / Ever [specific moment]? USE: it names a real frustration the video answers. AVOID: obvious yes/no questions, "did you know".

title: Story drop
summary: Start in the middle of the most intense moment, no setup.
body: [When], I [the most dramatic real moment]. / [The exact words someone said]. USE: a story with a strong moment. AVOID: starting at the start of the day, invented drama.

title: Straight promise
summary: Say plainly what the viewer will be able to do by the end.
body: How to [result] without [pain]. / [Result] in [N] steps. USE: the video teaches the full method. AVOID: promising more than it gives.

title: That's me
summary: Set up a situation so relatable the viewer sees themselves in it.
body: POV: [specific situation]. / When you [relatable moment]. USE: a shared experience of the audience. AVOID: situations everyone has.

title: Then vs now
summary: Put the before and the after side by side in one line.
body: I went from [real before] to [real after]. USE: a real change, ideally shown. AVOID: vague sides like "struggling" to "thriving".

title: This vs that
summary: Compare two options the audience is choosing between.
body: [A] vs [B]: which one actually [outcome]? USE: two real options and the user's verdict. AVOID: no clear winner.

title: Visual first
summary: Open on the most striking picture or action, before a word is said.
body: Open on the most striking real shot, then speak. USE: they can film something that stops the scroll alone; suggest it as a VISUAL line. AVOID: a visual that doesn't match the words.

title: DM me
summary: Invite the viewer to message the user for help.
body: DM me [word] if you want help with [the problem, in the client's words]. Fits service businesses and coaches.

title: Follow for more
summary: Ask for a follow, tied to what the viewer gets next.
body: Follow for more [specific topic or series]. Name what they get; "follow for more" alone is weak.

title: Comment a keyword
summary: Ask for a one-word comment in return for a real resource sent by DM.
body: Comment [WORD] and I'll send you [the resource]. Resource not named? Write a gap, like [your free guide].

title: Next part
summary: Bring the viewer back for the next episode or part.
body: Part [N] is [where or when]. / Follow to see what happens next. Fits series and stories in parts. Not "part 2 at X likes".

title: The offer
summary: Point to the user's product or service.
body: [Offer] helps [who] [get result]. [Where to find it]. Only the offer the user named. One step. No invented prices or deadlines.

title: Real question
summary: Ask a genuine question the viewer wants to answer.
body: [A specific question about their own experience or opinion]? Fits stories, opinions and lists. Avoid "comment YES"-style asks.

title: Save for later
summary: Ask the viewer to save it for the moment they will need it.
body: Save this for [the moment they'll need it]. Fits steps, lists and tools.

title: Send to a friend
summary: Ask the viewer to send it to a specific person it would help or describe.
body: Send this to the [specific person] who [situation]. Sends reach new people. Name a specific person.

title: Strong ending
summary: No ask. End on the line that lands, or loop back to the first line.
body: No ask. End on the lesson, the punchline, or a line that loops back to the opening. Fits stories, POVs and emotional videos. Key word last.
